title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is handwritten scratch work. Show-through from the other side is the typescript of 'Le groupe de Brauer III', §8: the l-adic sequences (8.3)–(8.7), which match the next-page transcription. The handwriting concerns the 'Poincaré–Hodge algebra' project in the cote title: graded algebras H^0..H^{2n} with Poincaré duality and a Lefschetz class L. Five strands can be reconstructed.

(1) Degree of a Lefschetz discriminant. Fix Betti numbers b_0, b_1, ..., b_n. The iterated Lefschetz maps are L^{n-i}: H^i -> H^{2n-i} (sketched as M^0 --L--> M^{2n}). Using the Poincaré-duality identification of top exterior powers (the 'ξ^{b_i} × ξ^{2n-2i}' line), each map has a determinant det(L^{n-i}|H^i). Scaling L -> λL multiplies this determinant by λ^{(n-i)b_i}. So the product Δ(L) = ∏_{i<n} det(L^{n-i}|H^i) is a homogeneous polynomial function of L of degree Σ_{i<n} (n-i) b_i = n b_0 + (n-1) b_1 + ... . For n = 2 this is 2b_0 + b_1, which is what is written. Δ(L) ≠ 0 exactly when L satisfies hard Lefschetz.

(2) The adjoint operator Λ as a rational function of L. In the sl_2-triple (L, Λ, grading), the scaling L ~ λL forces Λ ~ λ^{-1}Λ. First Grothendieck tries 'Λ = P(L' (Λ polynomial in L). He then corrects this to Λ = Ω(L) Δ(L)^{-N}: the matrix entries of Λ are polynomials in L divided by a power of the discriminant. That is correct, since Λ is obtained by inverting the maps L^{n-i}. In the language of the standard conjectures, Λ is a rational function of L that is regular on the Lefschetz locus Δ ≠ 0. Homogeneity of degree -1 constrains deg Ω = N·deg Δ - 1.

(3) Toy test algebra. Grothendieck writes down the graded algebra generated in degree 2 by L and L':
Z[L, L'] / (L^4, L'^2 - LL', L^2 L' - L^3, L^3 L').
He lists bases: H^0 = 1, H^2 = <L, L'>, H^4 = <L^2, LL'>, H^6 = <L^3>. He derives L'^3 = L'^2 L = L^2 L' = L^3. This is meant as a candidate 'cohomology of a threefold' with ranks 1, 2, 2, 1. (A labelling H^0..H^4 is also tried first.)

(4) Other model algebras. He considers 1 ⊕ V ⊕ (Sym^•(V) minus V), i.e. truncated symmetric algebras. He also considers a tensor product Z[L]/(L^4) ⊗ Z[L']/(L'^2 - ...), a product-type example. There are reductions marked with bars (L^2 = L̄, LL' = L̄', L̄'^2 = L̄'), apparently passing to a quotient.

(5) Purpose. These are experiments on the axiomatics of 'algebras of Poincaré–Hodge type'. The question is how Λ depends on L, and which small algebras satisfy duality plus Lefschetz.
errors: The test algebra Z[L,L']/(L^4, L'^2 - LL', L^2L' - L^3, L^3L') is NOT a Poincaré duality algebra. In the bases (L, L') of H^2 and (L^2, LL') of H^4, every product L·L^2, L·LL', L'·L^2, L'·LL' equals L^3, so the pairing H^2 × H^4 -> H^6 has rank 1. Put z = L - L'. Then L'z = 0 and z^3 = 0, so z^2 ≠ 0 in H^4 pairs to zero with all of H^2. Hard Lefschetz does hold for L: multiplication H^2 -> H^4 is an isomorphism and L^3 ≠ 0. The example thus separates Lefschetz from duality, though the page does not say whether this was intended.
Λ is first guessed as a polynomial P(L), which is wrong in general. Grothendieck himself corrects this to Ω(L) Δ(L)^{-N}.
Some lines are fragmentary ('Λ=P(L', the struck-out H^0..H^6 diagram), so the full intent is uncertain.

ideas.what: Discriminant Δ(L) = product of determinants of L^{n-i}: H^i -> H^{2n-i}, homogeneous of degree Σ(n-i) b_i in L; its nonvanishing is hard Lefschetz
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz discriminant / non-Lefschetz locus (complement of Lefschetz elements, Zariski open)
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in Kleiman 1968 and in the later Lefschetz-properties literature (Stanley 1980, Watanabe 1987; Harima–Migliore–Nagel–Watanabe 2003)
ideas.where_published: Not in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969) as far as known

ideas.what: Adjoint Lefschetz operator Λ is a rational function of L with denominator a power of the discriminant, homogeneous of degree -1
ideas.modern_name: uniqueness/rationality of the sl_2 completion (Jacobson–Morozov) of a Lefschetz operator
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck/Kleiman (Λ determined by L; algebraicity of Λ as conjecture B)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1969); Kleiman 1968

ideas.what: Small graded test algebras generated in degree 2 with two generators (ranks 1,2,2,1), and truncated symmetric/tensor-product models
ideas.modern_name: Artinian (Gorenstein) graded algebras with the strong Lefschetz property; toy cohomology rings
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stanley, Watanabe, Iarrobino et al. (1980s onwards)

missed.claim: Grothendieck experiments with small graded commutative algebras, checking Lefschetz behaviour and duality relations, in order to axiomatize 'Poincaré–Hodge algebras'. This prefigures the commutative-algebra study of Lefschetz properties of Artinian Gorenstein algebras. His explicit example satisfies hard Lefschetz but fails Poincaré duality.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precursor link between the standard-conjectures axiomatics (as in Kähler packages and combinatorial Hodge theory) and the later Lefschetz-property literature, but it is only scratch work.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine scratch computations. They give the degree of the hard-Lefschetz discriminant, show that Λ is rational in L, and test a toy algebra (which actually fails duality). The interest is in documenting how the Poincaré–Hodge axiomatics was explored; no new result appears.
transcription_corrections: The faint typed text visible is show-through from the reverse (Brauer III §8, sequences (8.3)–(8.7)). It is not part of this page's handwritten content.
'Λ=P(L' is an unfinished expression, later replaced by 'Λ = Ω(L) Δ(L)^{-N}'.
The last line should read roughly 'Z[L]/(L^4) ⊗ Z[L']/(L'^2 - L'')'; the stray symbol after (L^4) is a tensor sign.
'λ^{(n-i)b_i}' is the scaling factor of det(L^{n-i}|H^i) under L -> λL, consistent with the degree count n b_0 + (n-1) b_1 = ... (for n = 2: 2b_0 + b_1).
